source: NCERT Class XII, Fundamentals of Human Geography, Ch. 8 (Transport and Communication).

sections.heading: 1. Transport — Meaning and Modes
points: **Transport** = the movement of people and goods from one place to another; a key service linking production and consumption.
Modes: **land (roads, railways, pipelines), water (inland and ocean), and air**.
Efficient transport promotes trade, development and integration.

sections.heading: 2. Land Transport
points: **Roads** — flexible, door-to-door; major highways (e.g. the **Trans-Canadian, Pan-American, Trans-Siberian** routes).
**Railways** — carry heavy/bulky goods over long distances; dense networks in Europe, North America, India.
**Pipelines** — transport liquids/gases (oil, gas) efficiently over long distances (e.g. the Big Inch, USA).

sections.heading: 3. Water and Air Transport
points: **Water transport** — cheapest for bulky goods; **inland waterways** (Rhine, Danube, Ganga) and **ocean routes**.
Key **canals**: the **Suez Canal** (Mediterranean–Red Sea) and the **Panama Canal** (Atlantic–Pacific) — shorten sea routes greatly.
**Air transport** — fastest, costliest; vital for long distances, difficult terrain and perishable/valuable goods.

sections.heading: 4. Communication and Trade
points: **Communication** — transmitting information: **telecommunication, satellites, internet, mobile, mass media**.
The **internet and satellites** made a global information network possible (a 'shrinking world').
Transport and communication support **international trade** (the exchange of goods/services across borders).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Transport modes: land (road, rail, pipeline), water, air.
Trans-Siberian Railway (longest); pipelines carry oil/gas.
Suez Canal (Mediterranean-Red Sea); Panama Canal (Atlantic-Pacific).
Water = cheapest for bulky goods; air = fastest but costliest.
Internet/satellites = global communication ('shrinking world').

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Suez Canal** links the **Mediterranean and Red Seas**; the **Panama Canal** links the **Atlantic and Pacific**.
**Water transport is the cheapest** for heavy/bulky goods; **air is fastest, costliest**.
**Pipelines** carry **liquids and gases** (oil, gas).
The **Trans-Siberian Railway** is the longest railway.
